title: Canonical function-field algebra of a dominant integral-scheme morphism
statement: Let $X$ and $S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], both integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be dominant, meaning that its image is dense in $S$. Write $\eta_X,\eta_S$ for their generic points [def-sc-generic-point] and $k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}$, $k(S)=\mathcal O_{S,\eta_S}$ for their function fields [def-sc-function-field], using structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The canonical function-field algebra of $f$ is the $k(S)$-algebra structure on $k(X)$ whose structure homomorphism is the generic stalk map $f^\sharp_{\eta_X}:k(S)\to k(X)$, with the source identified by the equality $f(\eta_X)=\eta_S$ supplied by dominance. Thus the map is the actual pullback of germs, not an arbitrary field embedding.
